name: CSS
typing: dynamically checked at parse and computed-value time
summary: Declarative stylesheet language of the web: rules pair selectors (patterns over the document tree) with property declarations, and the cascade, inheritance and per-module layout algorithms turn them into presentation. Defined today as a large family of independently levelled W3C modules rather than one versioned specification.

level_notes.0: No reference implementation. The definition is exercised by the three browser style/layout engines (Blink, Gecko with Servo's Stylo, WebKit), by standalone parsers (rust-cssparser, PostCSS, CSSTree, Lightning CSS, tinycss2), layout libraries (Taffy) and by the shared web-platform-tests suite; the Bikeshed spec sources in w3c/csswg-drafts are listed as tooling. Chromium source is linked on chromium.googlesource.com because the GitHub mirror rate-limits raw fetches.
level_notes.1: There is no single "CSS specification" after CSS 2.1: the language is the set of modules listed in the current CSS Snapshot. Deep links point at the CSSWG editor's drafts (drafts.csswg.org / drafts.css-houdini.org), whose section anchors match the dated W3C TR publications; www.w3.org/TR links are the normative published versions.
level_notes.2: MDN is treated as secondary (explains the specs). Formal-semantics work on CSS layout is academic (Cassius, Meyerovich & Bodik) and listed here rather than at level 1 because it is not part of the definition.
level_notes.3: Rosetta Code has no meaningful CSS category; compatibility tables (caniuse, web-features) play the role of comparison tables.
